# Builtins and the Host API

What the language answers to, and what a host answers to. Two tables, and the
line between them is the whole of what Cove can do without being given
anything: a **builtin** is the language's own, evaluated in the process with no
capability asked for; a **Host operation** reaches outside it and is refused
unless the run was granted the capability it names.

| builtin methods | 97 |

| free builtins | 7 |

## Free builtins

Called on nothing, the way a declared function is. Every one of them binds its
own type parameters, because there is no receiver to read one off.

| name | kind | signature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Ok` | constructor | `Ok(value: T) -> Result<T, E>` |
| `Err` | constructor | `Err(error: E) -> Result<T, E>` |
| `Some` | constructor | `Some(value: T) -> Option<T>` |
| `Error` | constructor | `Error(message: String) -> Error` |
| `Shared` | constructor | `Shared(value: T) -> Shared<T>` |
| `assert` | assertion | `assert(condition: Bool) -> Result<Unit, Error>` |
| `assertEqual` | assertion | `assertEqual(actual: T, expected: T) -> Result<Unit, Error>` |

## Host API

Not builtins. Every operation below names a capability, is refused when the run
was not granted it, is charged against the run's Host-call budget, and appears
in a trace. A builtin does none of those things.

### `console`

Capability `console`.

| operation | capability | effect | cancellable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `println(String...) -> Result<Unit, Error>` | `console` | irreversible write |  |
| `print(String...) -> Result<Unit, Error>` | `console` | irreversible write |  |
| `eprintln(String...) -> Result<Unit, Error>` | `console` | irreversible write |  |
| `eprint(String...) -> Result<Unit, Error>` | `console` | irreversible write |  |
